correctness.rationale: A weighted-path hitting probability proof establishes the exact last-vertex formula with all positive denominators. Its derivative on the normalized resistance simplex is ((n-k)h[k-1]+k*h[k])/(n-1)^2. The homogeneous Jacobian kernel is the single alternating binomial vector, so rank is n-2, enabling analytic submersion and one-dimensional inverse fibers for every target near uniform. Endpoint start comparisons prove all-start rigidity; exact algebra gives the global n=4 class. The standalone checker independently solves rational visited-set chains for n=3..6, tests all starts, computes symbolic derivatives and ranks through n=10, and passes 551 equalities. Finite checks supplement rather than replace the proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the local inverse design theorem and binomial one-parameter nonidentifiability, not the known weighted-cycle forward termination formula. A 2000 paper by Mosbah-Saheb covers forward probabilities; this is expressly acknowledged. The 2026 motivating paper studies different homogeneity assumptions and lists position-dependent bias as future work. Two graph-classification sources assume unweighted transitions. A potentially implicit inverse assertion in the incompletely accessible 2000 primary article remains a significant residual risk; searches are not treated as novelty proof.

value.rationale: An identifiable inverse-design gap arises when last-coverage data are used to judge fairness on heterogeneous cyclic networks. The theorem determines the exact local dimension and tangent of the inverse map for every n, proves realizability of every near-uniform target law, exhibits arbitrarily disparate yet exactly fair conductances on four vertices, and proves all-source measurements restore a sharp rigidity guarantee. These are structural properties of the model rather than a small numerical improvement or a renamed forward probability calculation.
